source_anchor: MDN String.prototype.split / for...of iteration; CLRS §32.1 naive substring counting
prompt_text: Count how many times the character "a" appears in the string "banana" and print the integer. Expected output: "3".

exec_cell.code: const s="banana"; const ch="a"; let c=0; for(const x of s){if(x===ch)c++;} console.log(c);

candidate_responses.text: CORRECT: split-and-count idiom — text.split(target).length - 1 gives the same count.
candidate_responses.code: const text="banana"; const target="a"; const count=text.split(target).length-1; console.log(count);

candidate_responses.text: WRONG: loop bound is i<s.length-1, skipping the last character — misses the final "a" in "banana".
candidate_responses.code: const s="banana"; const ch="a"; let c=0; for(let i=0;i<s.length-1;i++){if(s[i]===ch)c++;} console.log(c);

candidate_responses.text: CARGO-CULT: variable named "occurrences" but uses indexOf which returns the FIRST index, not the count.
candidate_responses.code: const text="banana"; const target="a"; const occurrences=text.indexOf(target); console.log(occurrences);
